title: Earth Quake Alert
footnote: 3g/6g/8g are acceleration thresholds, not earthquake magnitude. Peak Force is the reference label: this program stores the highest triggered threshold, not a precise peak-force measurement. Test gestures in MakeCode; speaker audio depends on board hardware.

stages.title: Show an X when shaken
stages.concept: An event runs when a gesture is detected.
stages.adds: Add on shake. Put show icon X inside it.
stages.predict: What will appear when you shake the board?
observe: Shake the simulator: an X appears.
The X stays on until the display changes.
stages.question: Which block detects the shake?

stages.title: Choose the shaking levels
stages.adds: Replace on shake with 3g. Add separate 6g and 8g events.
stages.predict: Will 3g and 8g show the same response?
stages.question: Which event gives the strongest warning?

stages.title: Add warning sounds
stages.concept: Sound makes an alert easier to notice.
stages.adds: Keep the displays. Add a tone at 6g and a melody at 8g.
stages.predict: Which alert will play the longer sound?
observe: 6g: happy face and a short tone.
stages.question: How can sound help us notice an alert?
stages.focusNote: Replace the 6g and 8g handlers as shown. Keep the 3g handler unchanged.

stages.title: Repeat the strong warning
stages.concept: A repeat loop runs the enclosed blocks several times.
stages.adds: Wrap the 8g alert in repeat 3. Clear the LEDs and pause after each melody.
stages.predict: How many times will the 8g melody play?
stages.question: Which blocks are inside the repeat loop?
stages.focusNote: Replace only the 8g handler. Keep 3g and 6g unchanged. One melody now repeats three times.

stages.title: Store the detected level
stages.concept: A variable stores a value for later use.
stages.adds: Create MaxShake. Set it to 3000, 6000 or 8000 in the events. B displays it.
stages.predict: After 8g then 3g, what will B show?
observe: This version stores the latest level.
stages.question: Why did 3000 replace 8000?
stages.focusNote: Add the variable and B readout. Set 3000, 6000 and 8000 at the start of the matching handlers; 3g is shown.

stages.title: Keep only the highest level
stages.concept: An if condition chooses whether to replace a value.
stages.adds: Only set MaxShake when the new level is greater than the stored value.
stages.predict: After 8g then 3g, what will B show now?
observe: A smaller level cannot lower the record.
Restart resets the stored value to 0.
stages.question: What does greater than protect?
stages.focusNote: Replace each direct assignment with an if comparison. The 3g change is shown; use 6000 for 6g and 8000 for 8g.

stages.title: Reuse the comparison
stages.concept: A function packages code that several events share.
stages.adds: Move the comparison into updateMax(currentG). Call it with each level.
stages.predict: Will the highest reading change after this edit?
observe: B still shows the highest saved level.
stages.question: Why use one function in three events?
stages.focusNote: Create updateMax and replace each repeated comparison with a call. This excerpt shows the 3g change.

stages.title: Reset for a new test
stages.concept: A button event can reset the stored result.
stages.adds: Add Button A: set MaxShake to 0, clear screen, show the ready face.
stages.predict: After A, what will B show?
observe: A clears the saved level to 0.
New events begin a fresh record.
stages.question: Why reset before a new test?
stages.focusNote: Add this Button A handler. Keep the startup, gestures, updateMax function and Button B.

stages.title: Read the result in g
stages.concept: Dividing milli-g by 1000 converts it to g.
stages.adds: Change B to show Peak Force, rounded MaxShake / 1000, then g.
stages.predict: What will B show when MaxShake is 6000?
observe: A then B: the saved level is 0g.
stages.question: Why do we divide by 1000?
stages.focusNote: Replace the old Button B handler. Keep everything else. The result is the highest threshold, not exact force.

stages.title: Complete the earthquake alert
stages.concept: A busy flag prevents overlapping display and sound sequences.
stages.adds: Set busy before an alert or readout; clear it afterwards. Press A or B after the alert finishes.
stages.predict: Will another alert interrupt the melody?
observe: One alert sequence plays at a time.
When finished, A resets; B reports g.
stages.question: Why update the record before checking busy?
stages.focusNote: Final addition: guard each display/sound handler with busy. Full program shows all events and both buttons.
